saints.name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
saints.title: Abbot and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The great Cistercian abbot and preacher whose eloquence and sanctity swayed the whole of Christendom…
biography: Born near Dijon in 1090, Bernard entered the young reform monastery of Cîteaux in 1112, bringing thirty companions with him, and three years later was sent to found the abbey of Clairvaux, which he governed as abbot for the rest of his life. Under his leadership the Cistercian Order spread across Europe with astonishing speed.

Though he sought the quiet of the cloister, Bernard was drawn again and again into the affairs of the Church — healing a papal schism, opposing errors, and preaching the Second Crusade at the pope's command. His writings, glowing with love of Christ and of the Virgin Mary, earned him the title of the Mellifluous Doctor; he died at Clairvaux in 1153.
saints.knownFor: His preaching, mystical writing, and leadership of the Cistercians.

canonization.canonized: 1174 by Pope Alexander III; Doctor of the Church (1830)
